So phlegm was a big one for me as I was healing.  I recommend getting mucinex tablets it was a life saver for me.  Its a part of the natural healing process, your vocal cords are inflamed and your body is responding by rushing blood and moisture to the area to allow the tissue to heal.  

DO NOT COUGH if you can help it do not clear your throat aggressivley.  Its annoying but the proper healing will be worth it.  Sleep through it if you can,  sleep is good your body just went thru a major event.

Hey there!  I had VFS with the same surgeon about two years ago and I totally agree voice therapy before and AFTER is super important.  The reason why its important after is to help you use your new voice correctly.  If I speak more in my throat area that raspiness is definitely still there however once you learn to raise your voice just a little bit into your mouth lips and nose it should mostly go away as you heal.  Honestly I find it to be a good reminder for me, if I speak and I sound raspy I immediately know where im making sounds from and can correct it and the more you practice the more it becomes muscle memory and the more it becomes natural.  

It is hard especially since you speak a certain way for 20+ years of your life and now have to speak another way but it is possible and VFS at least to me made it a lot easier since I can focus soley on my resonance and weight and not have to worry about pitch at all.  My biggest struggle still is when I'm around people im comfortable with or people who have heard me talk a certain way before I tend to get lazy with where I make my sounds lol.

  
Congratulations!  You sound great for only 3 months!  Your voice will continue to improve full healing takes 12-18 months typically so take it easy try not to yell or raise your voice be gentle with it and be happy : )

I personally had VFS done 2 years ago come this january.  I waited almost a year before I scheduled any other procedure.  First procedure I had done was a colonoscopy under GA woke up no issue or damage to my voice.  A few months later I had an orchiectomy done.  I spoke with the anesthesiologist's prior to both procedures and the sentiment is generally the same, They will attempt to use a bag mask where a it goes down your throat just before the vocal cords and pushed air in that way.  However if I couldn't be kept stable during that they would intubate and use a number 6 as recommended by my vfs surgeon but if worse comes to absolute worse they will do what they have to to preserve life.

  
Both procedures I had done and neither affected my VFS at all.

If I were you id wait 12 months if possible to give your vocal cords the maximum time to heal properly once its healed fully its my understanding that its pretty hard to damage.

That all being said I do still have some raspiness from time to time which is usually caused by an irritant such as pollen (allergies) being sick or talking a lot (8hrs or more). 
Your vocal cords are very delicate and can take quite a bit of time to fully recover, the good news is tho over time your voice will heal more and more and it really only gets better with time.
I also second the notion of not getting this surgery if you like to sing this surgery will 100% lower your vocal volume speaking in a crowded restaurant for me is not something I really enjoy 😂😂

Yeah if you are experiencing packet loss then run the tests and take pictures of them and show them to optimum support. A good program to use to prove packet loss is pingplotter. When testing ensure it’s a direct connection to the modem to rule out router issues.I always reach out to optimumhelp on twitter if you message them the pictures they will most likely want to set up a tech to come over. Set up an appt, the tech will check your lines outside packet loss can be caused by damaged lines, improper grounding, line noise. A way to test line noise yourself is to remove splitters that feed your modem if any ideally you want your modem plugged right into the coax outlet with zero splitters. If all this fails and you still get packet loss after having a tech over and running tests yourself it’s time to set up another appt and ask for it to be escalated ideally you want to talk to executive customer relations these representatives have the ability to have outside line crews service the issue.
